dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Hey there! Wanna come "dig for treasure"?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: How did you end up setting up a stall here?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: *sigh* Well, it's a long story. I was once a Treasure Hoarder, doing some business near The Chasm. Uh, please, put your sword away. I've turned over a new life and gone legit.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Of course, I did have some Mora stashed away when I split from the crew, but it all went down the drain after a while due to... some circumstances. As such, I was forced to set up shop here and earn a little cash that way.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: See you.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Alright then. See ya!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Ya-hey, you'll miss out if you just walk about! Come on, try digging for some treasure instead!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: How about it? Are you interested?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is this, anyway? Do you mean that we can dig up treasure somewhere amongst these piles of dirt?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Of course... you might, ahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: These piles of earth are filled with anything from cabbages to ore. There's some truly good stuff in there, too!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good stuff, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Can't we just keep digging till we get the good stuff, then?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: No, of course not. Now, I'm not going to lie to you, or my name's not Old Chou! See, some piles of dirt also have explosives hidden within them. You can keep digging so long as you don't dig any of those up.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: But once you do, it's game over — game over!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Explosives? That sounds like a dangerous game we're playing here.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Oh, no worries, these were all pilfer— I mean, borrowed on the sly many years ago from the underground mining camps. They're definitely duds, right down to the last one!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: So, how about it? Want to have a go?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Start digging.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Where's the treasure, huh? You sure you're not cheating us?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: No, no, I would never do that! Now, your man Old Chou here's not a man of fancy birth, no sir, but I can at least claim to be an honorable person!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: You know what? C'mere, let me give you a hint for all your trouble.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: So, get this... the best stuff is always surrounded by the most explosives. For example, the four tiles around a treasure chest will all contain explosives!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Only two of the tiles around ore will contain those explosives, and the tiles that surround a tile with no treasure at all will most certainly be free of any danger.

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: So what I'm saying is, don't be too discouraged if you dig up a couple of explosives. There's light at the end of the tunnel — you'll see!

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Huh? Wow, you sure went through the whole lot really quickly. Um, g—give me a moment to reset the tiles, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: Just, ah, go busy yourself elsewhere for the time being while I get set up again... And no peeking during that time, you hear?

dialogues.speaker: Old Chou
dialogues.text: You'd like to go for another round? Well, you're a real good sport, make no mistake, but I can't set this game up with all my grand prizes in your pockets. You've got to wait for a while, if you don't mind.
